title: hotty Catalog
description: Keys, forms and focus for A2UI surfaces shown in a terminal: the hotty catalog of the hotty profile of A2UI. Mix it with the basic catalog component by component. Its names start with Hotty (components) and hotty (functions), so that none can be one A2UI adds later.
instructions:
These components and functions come from the hotty catalog: give each one "catalogId": "https://hotty.neuroplast.io/a2ui/v1/catalog". Everything else comes from the basic catalog. Every hotty component's name starts with Hotty, and every hotty function's with hotty; a name without the prefix is basic's.

1. HottyShortcut binds a key to its surface. Put it anywhere in the tree (it draws nothing). Give either `press`, the id of a Button on the same surface, or `action`. Write keys as myelin key names do, in lower case: the modifiers (super, ctrl, alt, shift, in that order), each followed by '+', then a physical key in snake case or a character: "ctrl+s", "escape", "alt+arrow_down", "f5", "shift+g" (a capital is shift with its letter; "G" would mean g). Write mod for the platform's command key (super on a Mac, ctrl elsewhere): "mod+s". Prefer keys with ctrl or alt that fields leave alone, such as ctrl+s or ctrl+r: while the user is typing in a field, it takes printable keys and its editing keys (ctrl+a, ctrl+e, ctrl+b, ctrl+f, ctrl+w, ctrl+u, ctrl+k, ctrl+d, ctrl+h, ctrl+p, ctrl+n, alt+b, alt+f, alt+d).

2. HottyForm wraps fields (TextField and the like, usually in a Column) and runs `onSubmit` when the user presses Enter in one of them. Do not add a submit Button just for Enter; a Button inside a HottyForm is still an ordinary Button. A Button whose action is the form's onSubmit is its default, the one Enter presses, and shows so.

3. To move the keyboard to a component, call hottyFocus(id) from a Button's action, or send callRendererFunction. hottyBlur() gives the keyboard back to the terminal.

4. To focus a component when the surface first appears, set "metadata": {"extensions": {"io_neuroplast_hotty": {"autofocus": true}}} on it.

5. To change what keys do in the text fields inside a component, set "metadata": {"extensions": {"io_neuroplast_hotty": {"keys": "ctrl+s=submit ctrl+k=program"}}} on it: each binding is key=action, and `program` leaves the key to HottyShortcuts.

6. HottyProgress shows how far a task has come: `value` from 0 to `max` (default 1, so a fraction; set max 100 for a percentage), and an optional `label` above the bar. Bind `value` to the data model and move it with updateDataModel as the task goes. Leave `value` out while the task runs but its progress is not known.

7. HottySpinner shows that something is under way: a `label` beside a spinner. Bind `active` to the data model and set it to false when the work is done, or replace the spinner with the result.

8. HottyTable shows rows of data: give `columns` (each a `key` into the rows, a `header`, and `align`: "end" for numbers) and `rows`, a list of objects, best bound to the data model. Set `rowKey` to the field that identifies a row, and bind `selected` to a path: the user's selection is written there. To act on the selected row, give `onActivate` an action whose context reads that path; it runs on Enter or a second click. Set `height` to scroll long tables.

9. HottyList shows items to pick from, a label and a line under it each: give `items`, a list of objects with `label`, `description` and `value` (what identifies the item), best bound to the data model, and bind `selected` to a path: the user's pick is written there. To act on it, give `onActivate` an action whose context reads that path; it runs on Enter or a second click. Set `filterable` to let the user type / and narrow the items by their labels, and `height` to show long lists a page at a time. For a nav, such as a settings screen's sidebar of pages, set `variant` to "compact": an item a row, with no status line.

10. HottyKeyHints is a help line: the keys the user can press now, those of the component with the keyboard and the surface's HottyShortcuts. Put one at the bottom of a surface that takes keys, and give each HottyShortcut a short `label` ("save", "quit") so that it shows there. The user presses ? for the full view.

11. HottyScrollView shows content taller than the room it has, in a box `height` rows tall that the user scrolls: give it a `child` (a long Text, say), or `lines`, a list of strings. For a log or a command's output, bind `lines` to a list in the data model, add each line by writing the next index with updateDataModel (/log/0, /log/1, …), and set `follow` so that the box shows the newest. Call hottyScrollTo(id, "start" or "end") to move it. For the body of a screen that scrolls between a head and buttons that stay, such as a settings page's sections, set `variant` to "plain": no box, only a scrollbar. Don't put a page that is the surface's content, such as a docs page in a HottyMarkdown, in a HottyScrollView: put it in the surface itself, which scrolls as a whole, as a web page does.

12. HottyCode shows source code, highlighted: give `code` and `language` (a name such as "go" or a file name such as "main.go"). Set `lineNumbers` for a file or an excerpt of one (with `startLine`), and `marks` to point at lines: {"line": 12, "kind": "error"}, or a range with `end`; kinds are highlight, added, removed, error and warning. Put a long listing in a HottyScrollView. Code inside prose can stay a fenced block in a Text (```python), which is highlighted too.

13. HottyDiff shows a change to code, as a review does: give `patch`, a unified diff of one or more files (git diff's output), or the `old` and `new` text of one file with its `file` name. Set `view` to "split" for the two sides next to each other. Bind `selected` to a path: the hunk the user picks is written there, as "path:line". To act on it (stage it, revert it, comment on it), give `onActivate` an action whose context reads that path; it runs on Enter or a second click. Big diffs belong in props rather than the data model, and in a HottyScrollView.

14. HottyTree shows nodes in branches that fold, such as files in folders or a site's sections: give `items`, a list of nodes, each with a `label`, a `value` (what identifies it), an optional `icon` (a name as HottyIcon takes) and `children`, best bound to the data model. Bind `selected` to a path: the user's selection is written there, and the branches it is in show open. Bind `expanded` to keep which branches are open, or give a list to open some at first. To act on a leaf, give `onActivate` an action whose context reads the selected path; it runs on Enter or a second click. For a filter field, bind a TextField's value and the tree's `filter` to the same path. Set `height` to scroll a long tree. For buttons that open or close every branch, call hottyExpandAll(id) or hottyCollapseAll(id) from their actions.

15. HottyIcon shows an icon the basic Icon's 59 names lack, by its Material Symbols name as Google Fonts writes it ("account_tree", "terminal"); use the basic Icon for those it has. For a shape of your own, give {"svgPath": …}, with `strokeWidth` for an outline one. A renderer may have only some of Material's icons, and shows a mark for the others.

16. To show icons on tabs or options, set "metadata": {"extensions": {"io_neuroplast_hotty": {"icons": …}}} on a Tabs, as a list of names, one per tab in order, or on a ChoicePicker, as an object from an option's `value` to its name. Names are as HottyIcon takes them. Terminals without graphics show the titles alone.

17. HottySwitch is an on/off switch for one setting, as a phone's settings show them: give a `label` and bind `value`, a boolean, to the data model, where the user's flips are written. Prefer it to a CheckBox for a setting that takes effect at once; keep the CheckBox for a choice that a form sends later, such as accepting terms. Set `disabled` (true, or bound to a path) while it cannot change; it and the switch's checks take a literal or a path, not a function call. Space, Enter or a click flips it: Enter on it does not submit a HottyForm.

18. HottyChart draws numbers on an axis: `kind` "line" (the default) for a trend over time, or "bar" for amounts by category. Give `values`, a list of numbers, or `series` for several, each a `label` and its `values`; and `labels`, one for each point (times, days, names). Bind values to a list in the data model and add a point by writing the next index (/cpu/42), and set `window` to keep the last points only, so that the chart slides as they arrive. The axis fits the values, from 0; set `min` and `max` to zoom in, and `height` for the plot's rows (8). Keep long series out of a surface with sendDataModel, which would send them back with every action.

19. HottySparkline is a trend in a few cells, with no axis: give `values`, bound as a chart's, and put it in a Row between a Text that names it and one with the latest value. Set `window` to keep it that many columns wide as values arrive, and `height` for a taller one.

20. HottyRangeSlider picks a range of numbers on one track, such as a price filter: give a `label`, `max` (and `min`, 0 by default), and bind `start` and `end`, each to a path of its own, where the user's moves are written. Set `steps` to snap both ends, as a Slider's. Each knob is a Tab stop, and stops where it meets the other. Set `disabled` (true, or bound to a path) while it cannot change; it and the checks take a literal or a path, not a function call. A basic Slider fills from `min` to its knob; for one whose chosen part runs from its knob to `max`, such as a minimum rating, set "metadata": {"extensions": {"io_neuroplast_hotty": {"fill": "end"}}} on it.

21. To let the user reorder a HottyList, HottyTable or HottyTree, set `reorderable`, bind its items (`rows`) to the data model, where the new order is written, and bind `moved` to a path, where each move is written ({"item", "from", "to"}, places with an `index`, in a tree a `parent`) before `onMove` runs: give onMove's context that path. The user drags an item to where a line shows it lands (in a tree also into a node that has `children`, even an empty list), or presses alt+arrow_up and alt+arrow_down; in a tree alt+arrow_left and alt+arrow_right move a node out of its branch and into the node above. Two of a kind with the same `dragType` take each other's items. For cards on a board, use a basic List of a template for each column, with "metadata": {"extensions": {"io_neuroplast_hotty": {"reorder": {"type": "card", "moved": {"@path": "/move"}, "onMove": …}}}}. To let the user drop something on any component (a ticket on a person), give the thing {"drag": {"type": "ticket", "value": {"@path": "id"}}} (a list's items carry their data, by its dragType) and the target {"drop": {"accepts": ["ticket"], "value": {"@path": "/dropped"}, "action": …}}: what is dropped is written to value's path, and the action runs.

22. To suggest values as the user types in a one-line TextField (commands, places, names), set "metadata": {"extensions": {"io_neuroplast_hotty": {"suggestions": {"options": {"@path": "/cities"}}}}} on it, the options a list of strings: the field shows those that start with what was typed, case aside, and Tab or → takes the first, or the one the user highlights with the arrows. To suggest from what was typed (a search), give suggestions an `onInput` action whose context reads the path the field's value is bound to ({"query": {"@path": "/city"}}): it runs at each change, and you answer by writing new options with updateDataModel; the field narrows the old ones meanwhile. onInput runs at every key, and on a surface with sendDataModel each one carries the whole data model, so keep the options there short. Set `list` to false where a list would cover what the user needs to see: the rest of a suggestion still shows faint after the caret.

23. To tell the user that something happened, call hottyToast from a Button's action, or send callRendererFunction: a toast, a short notice in the surface's top right corner, over what is there, that goes after `timeout` milliseconds (5000; 0 keeps it until the user dismisses it). Give `message` and `kind` ("info", the default, "success", "warning" or "error"); an `id` to replace a toast in place ("Uploading 3 of 10", then "Uploaded") or to take it away with hottyDismissToast({"id": …}); and `actionLabel` with `action`, an event, for a button on it ("Undo", "Retry"), whose context is read as the toast shows. `message` and the context take a literal or a path, not a function call. Don't toast what the user must act on to go on, or a field's error: show those in the surface. For a tooltip, give a component an `accessibility.description` ("Deletes the conversation for everyone"): a HottyKeyHints on the surface shows it while the pointer or the keyboard is on the component.

24. To ask a yes or no question ("Delete 3 files?"), there is no component: put the question in a Text, then a Row of two Buttons, Yes and No, each with an action of its own, and four HottyShortcuts: `y` and `n` whose `press` is Yes and No, and arrow_left and arrow_right with the same label ("move") whose actions call hottyFocus with Yes and with No. Set "metadata": {"extensions": {"io_neuroplast_hotty": {"keys": "arrow_left=program arrow_right=program"}}} on the Row, so that the arrows reach the shortcuts on a hotty host, and autofocus on the answer to give by default (No, before what cannot be undone). The Button with the keyboard is the one shown picked. Shortcuts are the surface's, so ask one such question a surface; while a text field has the keyboard it keeps y, n and the arrows. At the end of a HottyForm, give Yes the event of the form's onSubmit. For a yes or no the user sets and changes, use a HottySwitch or a CheckBox.

25. HottyTimer counts down and HottyStopwatch counts up, a `label` before the time. Give a timer its `duration` in milliseconds (300000 for five minutes) and `onTimeout`, an action that runs once when it gets to 0 (an event, or hottyToast to tell the user). Both count from when they first show, while `running` is true, the default; bind `running` to a path to start and stop them from the data model, where a timer that runs out writes false. For Start, Stop and Reset Buttons, or HottyShortcuts, call hottyStartTimer(id), hottyStopTimer(id), hottyToggleTimer(id) and hottyResetTimer(id) from their actions; a timer started once it has run out starts over. To read a stopwatch's time when an action runs (a lap, a submit), bind its `elapsed` to a path and read that path in the action's context: the time in milliseconds is written there before any action runs, and when it stops or is reset. Set `interval` to 100 to show tenths of a second, and `format` to "duration" to show 4m59s, as Bubble Tea writes a time, rather than the default 4:59. `duration` and `running` take a literal or a path, not a function call.

26. HottyPaginator turns pages, as a terminal app does: a dot for each page, the one shown marked, which the user turns with the left and right arrow keys or a click on a dot. To show a long List or Column a page at a time, make it the paginator's `child` and set `perPage`: it shows that many of the child's items, the page's, with the dots under them. To page data you hold, such as a search's results, give `pages` instead, bind `page` (from 1) to the data model, and give `onChange` an action whose context reads that path: it runs at each turn, and you answer by writing that page's items with updateDataModel. Set `displayStyle` to "numbers" to show "3/10" instead of dots.

27. HottyMarkdown shows long-form Markdown, such as a docs page, as GitHub does: give `text`. Its headings get GitHub's IDs, so a link to "#usage" scrolls to the heading "Usage" wherever it is on the surface, and a page split into several HottyMarkdowns keeps GitHub's numbering ("#usage-1" for the second). Quotes that start with [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING] or [!CAUTION] show as callouts, and HTML comments show nothing. A link with a scheme (https:, mailto:) opens as a Text's. To follow a relative link ("install.md", "api.md#errors"), bind `link` to a path and give `onLink` an action whose context reads that path: the link's href is written there when the user follows it, with a click or Tab and Enter, and you answer with the page it leads to. Put a page in the surface itself, not in a HottyScrollView: the surface scrolls, and a link to a heading scrolls it there. Keep Text for a line or a short paragraph.

28. HottyBigText shows a few words or a number in large letters, as a banner, a title screen or a score: give `text`, bound to the data model for a value that changes (a countdown's time, a score), `size` ("small", "medium", the default, or "large") and `align` ("center" for a title); set `shadow` for letters that cast one, as on a title screen. A terminal draws it in block letters that have A to Z, the digits and common punctuation: lowercase shows in capitals, accents are left off, and any other character shows as ?. Keep it to a line or two; for a heading over ordinary content, use a Text with "# " instead.

29. HottyQRCode shows a QR code for the user to scan with a phone: give `value`, the text it holds (a URL, or WIFI:T:WPA;S:name;P:password;; for a network), and a `label` that says what scanning it does. Keep the value short: a terminal draws one module of the code a column wide and half a row tall, so a long value makes a code wider than the terminal, and one too long for any QR code shows as an error. `errorCorrection` (L, M, the default, Q or H) trades size for robustness; keep M unless the code is small enough to afford H. Also give the value in words or as a link next to it for a user who cannot scan.

30. A longText TextField resizes from its corner when the user drags it, as a web textarea does, both ways by default. To allow only one way, or neither, set "metadata": {"extensions": {"io_neuroplast_hotty": {"resize": "vertical"}}} on it ("horizontal", "none").

31. HottyFilePicker lets the user walk a directory the program has granted, to pick a file: give `root`, the name of a root the program grants (a host grants its own filesystems by name; an agent cannot name a path outside one). Bind `path` to the data model, the directory shown (empty for the root): the picker writes it as the user walks in and out. The arrows move (the left one goes up, the right one opens a directory), Page Up and Page Down by the screen, Home and End to the ends, and Enter picks a file. Bind `selected` to a path and give `onPick` an action whose context reads it: the picked file's path, relative to the root, is written there before the action runs. Give `onChange` to hear a directory change, and `filter` to narrow the names. Set `height` to scroll a long listing. The agent never reads the filesystem: it sees the directories the user opens (`path`, `onChange`) and the file picked (`selected`, `onPick`), never a listing or a file's content.

32. To let the user step through a ChoicePicker's options in place, shown as "‹ staging ›", rather than pick from a list that opens, set "metadata": {"extensions": {"io_neuroplast_hotty": {"cycle": true}}} on one that picks one (mutuallyExclusive, not chips): the arrow keys or a click on its arrows step it, round from either end. It suits a few short options, such as an environment, a size or a theme; keep the list for many.

33. HottyPicker is a command palette: a query on top and the rows you rank for it. Bind `query`, `rows`, `selected` and `action` to the data model. The picker never filters: give `onQuery` an action whose context reads the query, and answer it by writing the rows, best first, each with a `value` and a `title`, and optionally a `group` ("Pane: Split"), a `detail`, `keys` (the keys you bind to it, such as "ctrl+b , r", shown at its right), a `description` (a short sentence, shown smaller on a line under the title), a `section` heading, `match` and `groupMatch`, the title's and the group's matched character ranges, an `icon` (a HottyIcon name, or an emoji) and a `footer` note (such as the row's id, shown muted at the footer's left while it is selected). A row's `actions` each have an `id`, a `title` and one of the keys enter, mod+enter, alt+enter, shift+enter or shift+delete: the first runs on Enter, and the footer says what each does for the selected row, Enter's and the panel key kept where it is short of room. Tab completes the query to the selected row's `complete`, else its title. Give `onAction` an action whose context reads `selected` and `action`. Set `panelKey` (such as "mod+k") to let the user list a row's actions, and `status` for what the last action said.

34. To colour a Text, an Icon or a HottyIcon by what it says (a status: working, failed, waiting), set "metadata": {"extensions": {"io_neuroplast_hotty": {"tone": "success"}}} on it: "muted", "accent", "success", "warning", "error" or "info". In a list's template, give a path instead ({"@path": "tone"}) and a tone in each item's data. The colour is a hint a terminal without colours drops: say the state in the words or the icon as well.

35. To show or hide a component as the data model changes (a section, a Reset button while there is something to reset), set "metadata": {"extensions": {"io_neuroplast_hotty": {"hidden": {"@path": "/reset/none"}}}} on it: while the value is true, it and what it holds show nothing and take no room. accessibility.hidden is not that: it only keeps a component from a screen reader, as for an icon beside words that say the same, and the component still shows.

36. For a screen that fills the room the surface has, as a settings page or a dashboard does, set "metadata": {"extensions": {"io_neuroplast_hotty": {"stretch": true}}} on the root Column, and a weight on the child that takes the rows left over, such as a HottyScrollView (weight 1), whose height is then the least it shows. Leave it out for a card or a form, which are as tall as what they hold.

37. To set the children of a Column apart, as a settings page sets its settings apart, set "metadata": {"extensions": {"io_neuroplast_hotty": {"gap": 1}}} on it: a blank terminal row between each two, in place of the kit's own spacing, which keeps a form's fields tight. On a Row, it is the columns between its children; 0 packs them tight. Use it, not a Divider, where items need only room between them.

38. To size a TextField or a DateTimeInput to the value it takes, such as a port's 5 digits or a path's 48 characters, set "metadata": {"extensions": {"io_neuroplast_hotty": {"width": 5}}} on it: the characters its value shows, where a one-line text field otherwise shows 32. Where fields share columns, give their Rows' children weights instead.

39. For a page's call to action, such as an onboarding's Continue or a sign-in's Sign in, set "metadata": {"extensions": {"io_neuroplast_hotty": {"size": "large"}}} on its Button: taller and wider on a hotty host, where a Button is otherwise as tall as a field. Set it on the Buttons in the same row too (Back, Skip), so that the row lines up. Keep forms, dialogs and cards medium, the default. In a terminal's cells every Button is a row tall.

40. HottyKeys draws keys as keycaps on their own, for a cheat sheet or an onboarding's keys: give `keys` in HottyShortcut's names, a sequence's keys apart by spaces ("ctrl+b v") and alternatives by "/" ("arrow_up/k"), and mod for the platform's command key. For a cheat sheet, put a Column of Rows, each a HottyKeys and a Text, and give each Row's two children the same weights (1 and 2, say), so that the Rows line up as a table's columns; pick the weights so that the HottyKeys' share holds the longest keys, since a HottyKeys keeps its keys whole and pushes its Text over where it is narrower. Bind `keys` to the data model where the user's keymap can change. It shows keys; it binds none: a key that does something is a HottyShortcut's.

41. To keep a Text on one line, as a list row's title, set "metadata": {"extensions": {"io_neuroplast_hotty": {"lines": 1}}} on it: where it is wider than the room it has, it is cut with …, at whatever width, font and terminal the user has, so don't cut titles yourself. A short one, such as a badge or a status, then never breaks. A larger count shows that many rows at most, the last cut with …. Leave it out for prose, which wraps.

HottyShortcut.description: Binds a key to its surface and draws nothing. When the key is pressed while its surface is the active one, it presses the Button named by `press`, as a click would and only if that Button's checks pass, or it runs `action`. A key that types a character with no modifier but Shift does nothing while a text control has the keyboard.

key.description: The key, named as myelin key names 0.1 do (hotty SPEC §10.4): the modifiers it needs, each followed by '+', then a physical key in snake case or a character, all in lower case. The modifiers are super, ctrl, alt and shift, in that order, and mod, the platform's command key (super on a Mac, ctrl elsewhere), which comes first. A capital is shift with its letter. Examples: "ctrl+s", "mod+s", "escape", "alt+arrow_up", "f5", "shift+g". tab and shift+tab move focus, and cannot be bound.

press.description: The id of a Button on this surface. The key presses it as a click would. A plain id, not a ComponentId: the HottyShortcut does not contain the Button.

action.description: What the key does, when it presses no Button.

label.description: What the key does, in a word or two, for a renderer that lists the keys a surface takes.

HottyForm.description: A container of fields. Enter in a text field inside it runs `onSubmit`, if the HottyForm's checks pass. Fields inside it commit their values before `onSubmit`'s context is resolved.

child.description: The form's content, usually a Column of fields.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyProgress.description: A progress bar: how far a task has come, as a bar and a percentage, under an optional label. Without a value it is indeterminate: it shows that the task runs, not how far. It does not take the keyboard.

value.description: How far the task has come, from 0 to max. Leave it out, or bind it to a path that is not set yet, while that is not known.

max.description: The value when the task is done. The default, 1, takes value as a fraction; 100 takes it as a percentage.

label.description: What the task is, in a few words, on a row above the bar.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottySpinner.description: Shows that something is under way, with no measure of how far: a spinner, then its label. It does not take the keyboard.

label.description: What is under way, in a few words.

spinner.description: The spinner's look, as Bubble Tea's spinners are named.

active.description: Whether it spins. Default true. One that does not spin shows its label alone, where it was.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyTable.description: A table: rows of data under a header row, one row selected at a time. The user moves the selection with the arrow keys or a click, and Enter (or a click on the selected row) runs onActivate. It takes the keyboard.

key.description: The field of each row this column shows.

header.description: The column's title in the header row.

width.description: The column's width in characters. By default, as wide as its header and its widest cell.

align.description: Where the cells' text sits: end for numbers.

rows.description: The rows: objects whose fields the columns name. Bind it to a list in the data model, so that rows change with updateDataModel.

rowKey.description: The field that identifies a row, such as "id". The selection is that field's value, so it stays on its row as rows come and go. Without it, a row is identified by its index ("0", "1", …).

selected.description: The selected row's identity (its rowKey field). Bind it to the data model: the user's selection is written there, and onActivate's context reads it from there.

onActivate.description: Runs when the user presses Enter on the selected row, or clicks it again. Its context should read the selection from the path selected is bound to.

reorderable.description: Whether the user moves the rows: drags one where a line shows it would land, or presses alt+arrow_up or alt+arrow_down to move the selected one a place. The rows are written where `rows` is bound, the moved one stays selected, and onMove runs. Nothing moves while a filter applies.

dragType.description: What the rows are, for drag and drop, such as "task". A component whose io_neuroplast_hotty.drop accepts the type takes one dropped on it, as its data. Two reorderable HottyTables of one surface with the same dragType take each other's.

moved.description: Bind it to a path: when the user moves an item, the move is written there before onMove runs: {"item": the item's rowKey, "from": {"index": 2}, "to": {"index": 0}}. Each place also has the `path` its list is bound to, which tells two lists apart.

onMove.description: Runs after the user moves an item, by a drag or the keys, once the rows are written: give its context the path moved is bound to. An item from another one runs the onMove of the one it went to, or else of the one it left.

height.description: How many rows the table shows at once; the rest scroll under the header. By default, all of them.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyList.description: A list of items to pick from: each a label, with a line of description under it, one selected at a time, under an optional title and a status line that counts them. The user moves the selection with the arrow keys or a click and turns pages, and, when it is filterable, types / and then text to narrow the items by their labels. Enter (or a click on the selected item) runs onActivate. It takes the keyboard.

items.description: The items: objects with a `label`, an optional `description` and a `value` that identifies the item. Bind it to a list in the data model, so that items change with updateDataModel.

label.description: What the item is called: its first line, and what a filter matches.

value.description: What identifies the item, such as an id. The selection is this value, so it stays on its item as items come and go. Without it, an item is identified by its index ("0", "1", …).

selected.description: The selected item's value. Bind it to the data model: the user's selection is written there, and onActivate's context reads it from there.

onActivate.description: Runs when the user presses Enter on the selected item, or clicks it again. Its context should read the selection from the path selected is bound to.

reorderable.description: Whether the user moves the items: drags one where a line shows it would land, or presses alt+arrow_up or alt+arrow_down to move the selected one a place. The items are written where `items` is bound, the moved one stays selected, and onMove runs. Nothing moves while a filter applies.

dragType.description: What the items are, for drag and drop, such as "task". A component whose io_neuroplast_hotty.drop accepts the type takes one dropped on it, as its data. Two reorderable HottyLists of one surface with the same dragType take each other's.

moved.description: Bind it to a path: when the user moves an item, the move is written there before onMove runs: {"item": the item's value, "from": {"index": 2}, "to": {"index": 0}}. Each place also has the `path` its list is bound to, which tells two lists apart.

onMove.description: Runs after the user moves an item, by a drag or the keys, once the items are written: give its context the path moved is bound to. An item from another one runs the onMove of the one it went to, or else of the one it left.

filterable.description: Whether the user can type / to filter the items by their labels, as they type. The best matches come first, and Escape shows every item again.

height.description: How many items the list shows at once; the rest go on pages, which the arrow keys turn. By default, all of them.

emptyText.description: What shows in place of the items when there are none. By default, "No items.".

variant.description: How it looks: "list", a status line under the title and the description under each label, which sets a list of things to pick apart; or "compact", an item a row with its description beside its label, no status line and no blank rows, for a nav: a sidebar's pages or sections.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyKeyHints.description: A help line, as a terminal app has one at its bottom: the keys the user can press now, each with what it does. It lists the keys of the component that has the keyboard (a list's arrows and filter, a field's Enter in a HottyForm) and then the surface's HottyShortcuts that have a label, and follows the keyboard as it moves. ? switches it to a full view in columns, which also lists a text field's editing keys. It takes no focus and sends nothing.

toggle.description: Whether ? switches between the help line and the full view. Turn it off where ? is the surface's own key.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyKeys.description: Keys drawn as keycaps on their own, as a HottyKeyHints draws each hint's keys, for a cheat sheet, an onboarding's keys or a menu's shortcut: each chord a cap, a sequence's caps in order, alternatives apart. Its caps are labelled for the user's system (Ctrl+B on Linux, ⌘B for mod+b on a Mac). It is as tall as a line of text and as wide as its caps. It takes no focus and sends nothing.

keys.description: The keys, in HottyShortcut's names: "ctrl+s", "mod+shift+p", "alt+arrow_up". A sequence's keys are apart by spaces ("ctrl+b v": ctrl+b, then v), and alternatives by "/" ("arrow_up/k"). A "/" alone, or after a modifier ("ctrl+/"), is the key.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyScrollView.description: A box of a fixed height whose content scrolls, as a pager or a log does in a terminal app: either a `child` (a long Text, a Column of cards), or `lines` of text as data. The user scrolls it with the arrows, Page Up and Page Down, Home and End, and the wheel; a scrollbar shows where it is. With `follow`, it starts at the end and stays there as lines arrive, until the user scrolls up, and again once they scroll back down.

child.description: The content to scroll. Give either `child` or `lines`.

lines.description: Lines of text to scroll, such as a log or a command's output. Bind it to a list in the data model and add a line by writing the next index (/log/42); the data model has no append. Keep it out of a surface with sendDataModel, which would send every line back with each action.

height.description: How many rows the box shows.

follow.description: Start at the end, and keep showing the end as the content grows, while the user is there.

wrap.description: Wrap lines longer than the box is wide. Without it they are cut, and the left and right arrows scroll sideways.

variant.description: How it looks: "box", filled and with corners, which sets a log or a listing apart from what is around it; or "plain", no box, only a scrollbar, for the body of a screen that scrolls between a head and buttons that stay, such as a settings page's sections.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyCode.description: Source code, highlighted for its language, as a code viewer shows it: optional line numbers and marked lines (a change's added and removed lines, a line with an error) in a gutter. It has no height of its own: put a long listing in a HottyScrollView. For code inside prose, a Text's fenced code block (```go) is highlighted too.

code.description: The code, its lines separated by newlines.

language.description: What the code is: a language's name or alias ("go", "python", "ts", "bash", "diff") or a file name ("main.go", "Dockerfile"). Without one, or for a language the renderer does not know, the code is shown plain.

lineNumbers.description: Show line numbers in a gutter.

startLine.description: The first line's number, for an excerpt of a longer file. Marks use the same numbers.

marks.description: Lines to mark, each with a sign in the gutter and a tint: `highlight` (a line to look at), `added` and `removed` (a change), `error` and `warning` (a problem). A later mark over the same line wins.

end.description: The last line of a range of marked lines, inclusive.

wrap.description: Wrap lines longer than the width. Without it they are cut at the edge (on a hotty host the code scrolls sideways).

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyDiff.description: A change to code, as a code review shows it: one or more files of hunks, each line numbered on its old side and its new side, signed + or -, highlighted for its language, and the words a changed line changes marked. Unified (one column) or split (old and new side by side). Give a `patch` (a unified diff, as git diff writes it), or the `old` and `new` texts of one file. The user moves between hunks with the arrow keys or a click, and Enter (or a click on the selected hunk) runs onActivate. It has no height of its own: put a long diff in a HottyScrollView.

patch.description: A unified diff of one or more files, as git diff or diff -u writes it. Its hunks are shown as they are, with the unchanged lines they hold.

old.description: Without a patch: the file's text before the change.

new.description: Without a patch: the file's text after the change.

file.description: Without a patch: the file's name, shown above its hunks and naming its language unless `language` does.

context.description: Without a patch: how many unchanged lines show around each change. Longer unchanged runs are folded.

language.description: What the code is, for every file: a language's name ("go", "python") or a file name. By default each file's own name says.

view.description: unified: removed and added lines in one column, as git diff shows them. split: the old side on the left and the new on the right, a changed line beside the line it replaces; where there is no room for two sides, the diff is unified.

lineNumbers.description: Show each line's numbers on its old and new sides.

wrap.description: Wrap lines longer than the width. Without it they are cut at the edge (on a hotty host the diff scrolls sideways).

selected.description: The selected hunk: its file's name and the first line of its new side, as "api/handler.go:12" (the line alone without a file name). Bind it to the data model: the user's selection is written there, and onActivate's context reads it from there.

onActivate.description: Runs when the user presses Enter on the selected hunk, or clicks it again: to stage, revert or comment on it. Its context should read the hunk from the path selected is bound to.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyTree.description: Nodes in branches that fold, such as files in folders or the sections of a site: each node a label with an optional icon, and a branch holds child nodes. One node is selected at a time; the branches it is in show open. The user moves the selection with the arrow keys or a click; the arrow right or a click opens a branch and the arrow left closes it. Enter on a leaf (or a click on the selected one) runs onActivate. It takes the keyboard.

items.description: The roots: nodes, each an object with a `label`, an optional `icon` and `value`, and `children`, a list of nodes like it. Bind it to the data model, so that nodes change with updateDataModel.

selected.description: The selected node's value. Bind it to the data model: the user's selection is written there, and onActivate's context reads it from there.

expanded.description: The values of the branches that show open. Bind it to the data model to keep the user's folding there; given as a list, it is how the tree starts.

filter.description: Text that narrows the tree to the nodes whose labels hold its characters in order, with the branches that lead to them and the nodes they hold. Bind it to the path a TextField writes, for a filter field over the tree.

onActivate.description: Runs when the user presses Enter on the selected leaf, or clicks it again; on a branch, Enter opens or closes it instead. Its context should read the selection from the path selected is bound to.

reorderable.description: Whether the user moves the nodes: drags one where a line shows it would land, or onto a node that has `children` (a list, empty or not) to put it inside, or presses alt+arrow_up or alt+arrow_down to move the selected one a place; alt+arrow_left moves it out of its branch, after it, and alt+arrow_right into the node above it, as its last child. The nodes are written where `items` is bound, the moved one stays selected, and onMove runs. Nothing moves while a filter applies.

dragType.description: What the nodes are, for drag and drop, such as "task". A component whose io_neuroplast_hotty.drop accepts the type takes one dropped on it, as its data. Two reorderable HottyTrees of one surface with the same dragType take each other's.

moved.description: Bind it to a path: when the user moves an item, the move is written there before onMove runs: {"item": the item's value, "from": {"parent": "docs", "index": 0}, "to": {"parent": null, "index": 2}}, the parent a node's value, null for the roots. Each place also has the `path` its list is bound to, which tells two lists apart.

onMove.description: Runs after the user moves an item, by a drag or the keys, once the nodes are written: give its context the path moved is bound to. An item from another one runs the onMove of the one it went to, or else of the one it left.

height.description: How many rows the tree shows at once; it scrolls to keep the selected node in view. By default, all of them.

emptyText.description: What shows when the tree has no node, or the filter leaves none. By default, "Nothing here.".

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyIcon.description: An icon by its Material Symbols name (Sharp, filled), for the icons the basic Icon's 59 names lack, or a path of your own, filled or stroked. It is as tall as the text around it and takes its colour. A name the renderer has no shape for shows as a mark in its place. It does not take the keyboard.

name.description: The icon's Material Symbols name, in snake_case as Google Fonts writes it: "account_tree", "terminal", "rocket_launch". The basic Icon's 59 are here too, by Material's names ("account_circle", "play_arrow"). Or {"svgPath": …}, a shape of your own.

svgPath.description: Path data in a 24 by 24 box, as an svg path's d: commands and numbers only, at most 8 KB.

strokeWidth.description: Stroke the path this wide, in the box's units, instead of filling it: an outline icon's path, such as Lucide's (2).

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottySwitch.description: An on/off switch for one setting, as a phone's settings have them: a track with a knob at its end, the knob at the right and coloured while on. Space, Enter or a click flips it, and the new value is written where `value` is bound. It takes the keyboard, unless it is disabled.

label.description: What it turns on or off, beside the switch: "Wi-Fi", "Notifications". Without one, give accessibility.label.

value.description: Whether it is on. Bind it to the data model: the user's flips are written there.

disabled.description: While true, the switch shows faint, does not flip and does not take the keyboard. Bind it to disable the switch while another setting rules it out.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyRangeSlider.description: A range of numbers on one track, as a price filter has it: two knobs, the start's and the end's, and the range between them filled. Each knob takes the keyboard, a Tab stop of its own: the arrows move the one that has it, Home and End take it to the ends, and a knob stops where it meets the other. A click on the track moves the nearer knob there, and a drag moves it with the pointer. Each end is written where it is bound.

label.description: What the range is of, beside the track: "Price", "Year". Without one, give accessibility.label.

start.description: The range's lower end. Bind it to the data model: the user's moves are written there.

end.description: The range's upper end, not below start. Bind it as start, to a path of its own.

min.description: The lowest value either end takes.

max.description: The highest value either end takes.

steps.description: The number of discrete divisions of the range, as a Slider's: both ends snap to them.

disabled.description: While true, the knobs show faint, do not move and do not take the keyboard.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyChart.description: A chart of numbers on an axis: a line chart, in braille dots in a terminal and a line on a hotty host, or a bar chart, its bars in eighths of a row. Labelled ticks up its side, the points' labels under it, and a legend when it has several series or a named one. It does not take the keyboard.

kind.description: line joins the values, for a trend over time; bar draws a bar for each value, for amounts by category, several series side by side.

values.description: The values of a chart of one series, oldest first: numbers, and a null where one is missing. Bind it to a list in the data model, and add a point by writing the next index (/cpu/42): the data model has no append.

series.description: Several series, each a `label` for the legend and its `values`, which may each be bound to a list in the data model: {"label": "cpu", "values": {"@path": "/cpu"}}. Give either `values` or `series`.

labels.description: A label for each point, in the same order: times or dates for a line, categories for bars. A line chart shows a few of them under its axis, a bar chart each under its bars.

min.description: The value at the bottom of the axis. By default the axis fits the values: from 0 when they are all positive (or all negative), to a round number past the furthest.

max.description: The value at the top of the axis. A value outside min and max is drawn at the edge.

height.description: How many rows tall the plot is, without its axis, labels and legend.

window.description: How many points the chart holds: the last ones, the newest at the right edge, so that a series that grows slides along. By default it shows all of them, across its width.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottySparkline.description: A sparkline: a trend in a few cells, a column for each value, rising from the bottom in eighths of a row, with no axis and no labels. Put it in a Row beside a Text that names it and one with the latest value. It does not take the keyboard.

values.description: The values, oldest first: numbers, and a null where one is missing. Bind it to a list in the data model, and add a value by writing the next index (/load/42): the data model has no append.

min.description: The value at the bottom. By default 0, or the lowest value when that is below 0.

max.description: The value at the top. By default the highest value.

height.description: How many rows tall it is.

window.description: How many values it shows, a column each: the last ones, the newest at the right edge, so that it keeps its width as values arrive. By default, as many as it has.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyTimer.description: A countdown, as a kitchen timer has it: the time left after an optional label, ticking down to 0, when it stops and runs onTimeout. It counts while `running` is true, from when the surface first shows it, whether it is in sight or not. It does not take the keyboard: Buttons and HottyShortcuts start, stop and reset it with hottyStartTimer, hottyStopTimer, hottyToggleTimer and hottyResetTimer.

label.description: What it times, in a few words, before the time: "Tea", "Retrying in".

duration.description: How long it counts down, in milliseconds: 300000 for five minutes. A new duration changes the time left, not the time counted; bound to a path that holds nothing, it does not count.

running.description: Whether it counts. Default true. Bind it to a path to start and stop it from the data model; the timer functions write it there too, and false when it runs out. Set true once it has run out, it starts over from its duration.

interval.description: The step its time shows in, in milliseconds: 1000 (the default) shows whole seconds, 100 tenths of a second. The time left is rounded up, so it shows 0 just as it runs out.

format.description: How the time is written: "clock" (the default) as a clock shows it (4:30, 0:09.5, 1:02:03), "duration" as Bubble Tea writes it (4m30s, 9.5s, 0s).

onTimeout.description: Runs once when it gets to 0, after `running` is set false: an event for the agent, or a function such as hottyToast. It runs without the user's activation, so it cannot open a URL.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyStopwatch.description: A stopwatch: the time counted up from 0, after an optional label. It counts while `running` is true, from when the surface first shows it, whether it is in sight or not. It does not take the keyboard: Buttons and HottyShortcuts start, stop and reset it with hottyStartTimer, hottyStopTimer, hottyToggleTimer and hottyResetTimer.

label.description: What it times, in a few words, before the time: "Elapsed", "Lap".

running.description: Whether it counts. Default true. Bind it to a path to start and stop it from the data model; the timer functions write it there too.

elapsed.description: Bind it to a path to read the stopwatch's time in an action's context, as a lap or a submit needs: the time counted, in whole milliseconds, is written there when it stops, when it is reset, and before any action of the surface runs. It is written, not read: writing the path does not set the time.

interval.description: The step its time shows in, in milliseconds: 1000 (the default) shows whole seconds, 100 tenths of a second.

format.description: How the time is written: "clock" (the default) as a clock shows it (4:30, 0:09.5, 1:02:03), "duration" as Bubble Tea writes it (4m30s, 9.5s, 0s).

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyPaginator.description: Pages, as a terminal app turns them: a dot for each page, the one shown marked, or the page of how many ("3/10"). The user turns them with the left and right arrow keys, Page Up and Page Down, Home and End, or a click on a dot. With a `child`, a List, Column or Row, it shows `perPage` of the child's items at a time, the page's, with the dots under them; without one, give `pages`, and the agent sends each page's data when onChange runs. It takes the keyboard.

child.description: What to show a page at a time: a List, Column or Row, whose children are the items, such as a List of a template for a list in the data model. Give either `child` or `pages`.

perPage.description: How many of the child's items a page shows.

pages.description: How many pages there are, without a child: pages of data the agent holds, such as a search's results, which it sends a page at a time.

page.description: The page shown, from 1 (the default). Bind it to the data model: the user's turns are written there, and writing it shows that page.

displayStyle.description: How the pages show: "dots", a dot for each page, the one shown marked; or "numbers", the page shown of how many, "3/10". Dots that do not fit show as numbers.

onChange.description: Runs when the user turns a page, once `page` is written: its context should read the path page is bound to. Answer with the page's data.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyMarkdown.description: Long-form Markdown, such as a docs page, as GitHub shows it: headings with GitHub's IDs, alerts (quotes that start with [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING] or [!CAUTION]) as callouts, fenced code highlighted, tables, and images (their alt text in a terminal); HTML, comments among it, shows nothing. A link with a scheme opens as a Text's. A link without one goes in place: a #fragment that names a heading on the surface scrolls to it; any other is written to `link`, and onLink runs. Its links in place are Tab stops, which Enter or a click follows.

link.description: Where the href of a link in place the user follows is written, as the Markdown has it ("install.md", "api.md#errors", or a #fragment no heading on the surface has). Bind it to the data model: onLink's context reads it from there.

onLink.description: Runs when the user follows a link in place, once `link` is written: its context should read the path link is bound to. Answer with the page it leads to.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyBigText.description: Text in large letters, as a banner, a title screen or a number read from across the room has it: in a terminal, block letters a few rows tall drawn with block characters; on a hotty host, large display type. A terminal's letters are A to Z (lowercase shows in capitals), the digits and common punctuation. It does not take the keyboard.

text.description: The text: a word or a few, a name, or a number such as a score or a time. A line break (\n) starts a new line, and a line too long for its room wraps between words.

size.description: How large: in a terminal, letters 3 (small), 4 (medium) or 5 (large) rows tall.

align.description: Where each line goes across the room it has: "center" for a title screen.

shadow.description: Whether the letters cast a shadow down and to the right, a title screen's 3D look: in a terminal, in the border's colour, the letters a column further apart.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyQRCode.description: A QR code that a phone's camera reads: a link, a pairing code, a Wi-Fi network or a short text to carry from the screen to the phone. In a terminal it is drawn with block characters, dark on white whatever the terminal's colours; on a hotty host it is a picture. It does not take the keyboard.

value.description: The text the code holds, as the phone reads it: a URL, or text in a scheme a phone acts on (WIFI:T:WPA;S:name;P:password;; for a network, mailto:, tel:). The shorter, the smaller the code: a short URL draws 30 to 40 columns wide and 15 to 20 rows tall in a terminal. Empty, nothing is drawn.

errorCorrection.description: How much of the code may be hidden or damaged and still read: L about 7%, M 15%, Q 25%, H 30%. A higher level makes a larger code for the same value; the code gets a higher level than this where its size holds one at no cost.

label.description: A caption under the code, such as "Scan to open on your phone".

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyFilePicker.description: A directory the user walks to pick a file, listing a root the program has granted: a terminal app's open dialog. The agent never reads the filesystem: it learns only the directories the user opens (written to `path`) and the file picked (written to `selected`), as the data model or an action's context brings them, never a listing or a file's content. It takes the keyboard.

root.description: The name of a root the program granted. The picker lists no directory outside it, and the agent cannot name one.

path.description: The directory shown, relative to the root, slash-separated ("" is the root). Bind it to the data model: the picker writes it as the user walks into and out of directories, so the program follows along. A literal is the directory it starts in.

selected.description: The path the user picked, relative to the root, written where this is bound when a file is picked. An action's context reads it; an action carries no payload of its own.

filter.description: A case-insensitive substring: only the names that hold it are listed.

onPick.description: Runs when the user picks a file, after its path is written to `selected`; the context reads that path. A directory is opened, not picked.

onChange.description: Runs when the directory shown changes (the user opens one or goes up), after the directory is written to `path`; the context reads that path.

height.description: The entries a screen shows, 0 or absent for all of them. More than this scroll.

emptyText.description: What shows when the directory has nothing (or the filter leaves nothing): "Empty." without it.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

HottyPicker.description: A command palette's picker: a query the user types on top, the rows the agent ranks for it under it, and actions on the selected row by keys that type nothing. The picker never filters or ranks: it writes the query and runs onQuery after each change, and the agent answers by writing new rows. The arrow keys (Control+p and Control+n too) and Page Up and Page Down move the selection, a row's actions run by their keys, and panelKey opens the selected row's actions as a list. It takes the keyboard.

query.description: What the user types. Bind it to the data model: the picker writes it as the user types, then runs onQuery. A literal is the query it starts with.

onQuery.description: Runs after each change the user makes to the query: give its context the path query is bound to, and answer by writing rows (and, if you like, selected).

placeholder.description: What the empty query shows, faint.

chip.description: A word or two before the query, such as a command already chosen ("pane.split ▸") or a scope (">").

rows.description: The rows, best first, as the agent ranked them for the query: the picker shows them in this order. Bind it to a list in the data model, so that rows change with updateDataModel.

value.description: What identifies the row, such as an id. The selection is this value, so it stays on its row as rows come and go.

complete.description: What Tab fills the query with while the row is selected, such as a command's name to type arguments after. By default, its title.

group.description: What the row belongs to, shown before its title as "Group: Title", muted, as a command's category.

detail.description: A word or two after the title, muted: what the row would act on.

icon.description: An icon before the row's name: a name as HottyIcon's, a Material Symbols name such as "terminal" (or one of the basic Icon's names), or a character of your own, such as an emoji, drawn as it is. Where some rows have one, a row without one has a blank as wide, so that names line up.

keys.description: The keys that run the row where you bind them, such as a command's binding, shown at the row's right, muted: key names as HottyShortcut's, a sequence apart by spaces ("ctrl+b , r"). The picker shows them and does not take them.

description.description: A short sentence on a line under the title, smaller and muted: what the row does. A row without one takes a line.

section.description: A heading shown above the row when it differs from the row before's, such as "Recently used".

match.description: Where the query matched the title, to draw those characters out: [from, to) pairs of character offsets in the title.

groupMatch.description: Where the query matched the group, as match is for the title: [from, to) pairs of character offsets in the group.

footer.description: A note at the footer's left, muted, while the row is selected, such as the row's id ("pane.split"). Where the footer is short of room, it is cut, after Enter's action and the panel key have theirs.

actions.description: What the user can do to the row, each on a key: the first is the one Enter runs, whatever key it names. They show in the picker's footer while the row is selected, each with its title, not on the row: Enter's at the right, then the others, then the panel key. Where they don't all fit, the last ones go first; Enter's and the panel key stay, and the panel lists every one with its key.

id.description: What identifies the action: it is written to `action` when the action runs.

title.description: What the action does, in a few words: "Open", "Close pane".

key.description: The key that runs it on the selected row. A picker's action keys type nothing, so that every other key goes to the query: mod is Control, or Command on a Mac.

selected.description: The selected row's value. Bind it to the data model: the picker writes it as the user moves the selection, and before an action runs. When it names no row, the first row is selected.

action.description: Bind it to a path: when the user runs an action, its id is written there ("" for Enter on a row with no actions), and the row's value to selected, before onAction runs.

onAction.description: Runs when the user runs an action on the selected row, by its key, Enter, or from the actions panel: give its context the paths selected and action are bound to.

panelKey.description: The key that opens the selected row's actions as a list, each with its key: the arrows move in it, Enter runs one, and Escape or the key again closes it. Without it there is no panel. "mod+k" is Raycast's.

keep.description: What a row keeps where its text and its keys don't both fit: "detail", the default, its whole text, so that only the selected row shows its keys; or "keys", on every row, its text cut for them, its title first, then its detail. A picker of key bindings keeps keys.

status.description: A line under the query: why the last action failed, or what it answered. It stays one line, cut with an ellipsis where it is wider than the picker. Empty, it does not show.

statusKind.description: "error" for a status that says what went wrong, drawn as an error; anything else ("info", the default) for one that says what an action answered. Bind it beside status, so the agent says which with each.

loading.description: Whether rows are still to come for the query.

emptyText.description: What shows in place of the rows when there are none. By default, "No matches.".

height.description: How many lines the rows (and their headings) take at most; the rest scroll. By default, 10.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column, as CSS 'flex-grow'.

hottyFocus.description: Gives the keyboard to a component of the surface: the user's next keys go to it. On a hotty host it is a=focus.

id.description: The id of the component to focus. A template's component takes the instance in the caller's scope.

hottyBlur.description: Gives the keyboard back to the terminal. A field that had it commits its value first. On a hotty host it is a=blur.

hottyScrollTo.description: Scrolls a HottyScrollView to its start or its end. A view with `follow` that is scrolled to its end shows new lines as they arrive again, as it does once the user scrolls there; one without stays where it is when lines arrive.

id.description: The id of the HottyScrollView. A template's component takes the instance in the caller's scope.

hottyExpandAll.description: Opens every branch of a HottyTree, as the user would one by one: where `expanded` is bound, every branch's value is written there.

id.description: The id of the HottyTree. A template's component takes the instance in the caller's scope.

hottyCollapseAll.description: Closes every branch of a HottyTree: where `expanded` is bound, an empty list is written there. A selection inside a branch moves to the root it is in, so that only the roots show.

id.description: The id of the HottyTree. A template's component takes the instance in the caller's scope.

hottyToast.description: Shows a toast: a short notice in a corner of the surface, over what is there, that goes after a while. Toasts stack, the newest nearest the corner, and a newer one takes the oldest's place once there are five. The user dismisses one with a click on it or Escape, and picks its action, if it has one, with a click on it or Tab and Enter; its time does not count while the pointer or the keyboard is on it.

message.description: What happened, in a short sentence: "Draft saved", "Could not reach the server".

kind.description: What the toast says, which its mark and its colour show: news, something done, something to watch, something that failed.

timeout.description: How long it shows, in milliseconds, not counting while the pointer or the keyboard is on it. 0 keeps it until the user dismisses it or hottyDismissToast takes it.

id.description: A name for the toast. A toast shown with the id of one there takes its place, its time starting again ("Uploading 3 of 10", then "Uploaded"); hottyDismissToast takes it by its id; and its action's message names it as its sourceComponentId. Without one, the renderer names it.

actionLabel.description: The action's label, a word or two: "Undo", "Retry", "View".

action.description: What picking the action does: an event for the agent, as a Button's. Its context is read when the toast shows, so that it names what the toast is about even once the data has moved on. The toast goes once it is picked.

surfaceId.description: The surface it shows on. By default the caller's, or, when the agent calls it, the surface that has the keyboard, else the first one made.

hottyDismissToast.description: Takes a toast away before its time: the one hottyToast showed with this id, on the caller's surface, or on any when the agent calls it. A toast gone already is no error.

id.description: The toast's id, as hottyToast was given it.

hottyStartTimer.description: Starts a HottyTimer or a HottyStopwatch: it counts on from where it stopped, and a HottyTimer that has run out starts over from its duration. Where its `running` is bound, true is written there.

id.description: The id of the HottyTimer or HottyStopwatch. A template's component takes the instance in the caller's scope.

hottyStopTimer.description: Stops a HottyTimer or a HottyStopwatch where it is. Where its `running` is bound, false is written there.

id.description: The id of the HottyTimer or HottyStopwatch. A template's component takes the instance in the caller's scope.

hottyToggleTimer.description: Stops a HottyTimer or a HottyStopwatch that is running, and starts one that is not, as hottyStopTimer and hottyStartTimer do: for one key or Button that does both.

id.description: The id of the HottyTimer or HottyStopwatch. A template's component takes the instance in the caller's scope.

hottyResetTimer.description: Takes a HottyTimer back to its whole duration, or a HottyStopwatch back to 0. One that runs counts on from there; one that is stopped stays stopped.

id.description: The id of the HottyTimer or HottyStopwatch. A template's component takes the instance in the caller's scope.

label.description: What the node is called: its row, and what a filter matches.

icon.description: An icon before the label, as HottyIcon names one: a Material Symbols name such as "folder" or "description" (or one of the basic Icon's names).

value.description: What identifies the node, such as a path. The selection and expanded are these values, so they stay on their nodes as nodes come and go. Without it, a node is identified by its place ("0", "0.2", …).

children.description: The nodes in this one, which makes it a branch. An empty list makes a branch with nothing in it yet, such as an empty folder, which a reorderable tree moves nodes into.

href.description: Where the node leads, in a docs site's navigation: a page's path or a #fragment, as a HottyMarkdown's links have them.

label.description: What the series is: its name in the legend.

values.description: Its values, oldest first: numbers, and a null where one is missing. Bind it to a list in the data model to add points by index.

io_neuroplast_hotty.description: The kit's extension: "metadata": {"extensions": {"io_neuroplast_hotty": {…}}} on a component. Renderers that do not know it ignore it.

autofocus.description: The component takes the keyboard as soon as it is there, until the surface has given it to anything.

keys.description: A keymap for the text fields inside the component, and itself if it is one: bindings key=action, white space between them, as hotty's data-keys ("ctrl+s=submit ctrl+k=program"). A key bound to `program` reaches the HottyShortcuts from any element inside that has the keyboard, a Button too, where a hotty host would scroll with it ("arrow_left=program").

fill.description: On a Slider: "end" fills it from its knob to its max, for a chosen part that runs to the end (a minimum rating); "start", the default, from its min to its knob.

cycle.description: On a ChoicePicker that picks one, shown as checkboxes (a select): its options stepped through in place, "‹ staging ›", round from either end, by the arrow keys or a click on its arrows, with no list.

resize.description: On a longText TextField: the axes its corner resizes it along when the user drags it, as a web textarea's. "both" is the default.

tone.description: On a Text, an Icon or a HottyIcon: the colour its glyphs take, by the role it names: "muted", "accent", "success", "warning", "error" or "info" (any other value leaves it its own). A literal, or a path, relative in a template, so that each item's comes from its data. It is colour alone: say what it means in the words or the icon too.

hidden.description: On any component: while true, it and what it holds show nothing, take no room and no focus. A literal, or a path, so that a write to the data model shows or hides it. accessibility.hidden is not this: it keeps a component from a screen reader only, and the component still shows.

stretch.description: On the surface's root: it is as tall as the surface, and the rows its content leaves go to its weighted children (a weighted HottyScrollView pages at the rows it gets, its height the least), or as its justify says. Elsewhere it does nothing.

gap.description: On a Column, a Row or a List: the whole terminal rows between its children, or a Row's columns, in place of the kit's own spacing. 1 sets each a blank row apart, as a settings page's settings; 0 packs them tight. At most 8.

width.description: On a TextField or a DateTimeInput: the characters its value shows, in terminal columns, in place of the kit's own (a one-line text field's 32, a DateTimeInput's form). Less where the field has less room. A longText starts this wide, and its grip resizes it.

lines.description: On a Text: the most rows it shows, the last cut with … where it has more. 1 keeps it on one line, as a list row's title, cut at the room it has, and a short one, such as a badge, whole. The full text stays in the data model; a Text without it wraps.

size.description: On a Button: "large" for a page's call to action, taller and wider on a hotty host, borderless ones too, so that a row of them lines up; "medium", the default, as tall as a field. In cells every Button is a row tall.

icons.description: Icons for a Tabs' titles, a name a tab in order, or for a ChoicePicker's options, an object from an option's value to its name. Names are HottyIcon's.

suggestions.description: On a one-line TextField: suggestions as the user types. Those of the options that start with the value (case aside) show in a list over what is under the field, and the rest of the first, or of the one highlighted, shows faint after the caret: Tab or → at the end takes it, ↓ and ↑ (ctrl+n, ctrl+p) move through the list, Enter picks the one highlighted, Escape closes it. A taken suggestion is the field's value, as written.

options.description: What may complete the value: a list of strings, best bound to the data model, where the agent may rewrite it as it hears what was typed (onInput). The field shows those that start with its value.

onInput.description: Runs after each change the user makes to the value, a taken suggestion too: give its context the path the value is bound to, and answer by writing new options.

list.description: Whether the list shows (default true). False shows only the rest of a suggestion faint after the caret, which ↓ and ↑ change: for a field typed through rather than picked from, or where a list would cover what the user needs to see.

drag.description: The component is a drag source: the user drags it onto a component whose drop accepts its type.

value.description: What it carries, resolved in its scope: {"@path": "id"} in a template's item is the item's id.

drop.description: The component is a drop target: the user drops onto it a drag source, or an item of a list with a dragType, whose type it accepts. What that means is the action's.

value.description: Where what is dropped is written before the action runs: a drag source's value, or a list's item's data (a HottyTable's row, a HottyList's item, a HottyTree's node, a List's item).

action.description: Runs on the drop, in the component's scope: give its context the path value is bound to.

reorder.description: On a List whose children are a template: the user moves its items, as a reorderable HottyList's, by a drag or by alt+arrow_up and alt+arrow_down on the item that has the keyboard. The template's list is written, then onMove runs.

type.description: What the items are, such as "card": Lists with the same type take each other's items, and a drop target that accepts it takes one, as its data.

moved.description: Where the move is written before onMove runs: {"item": the item's data, "from": {"path": "/board/todo", "index": 2}, "to": {"path": "/board/doing", "index": 0}}.

onMove.description: Runs after a move. An item from another List runs the onMove of the one it went to, or else of the one it left.
